      Samsung

      We’re thrilled to hear that your switch to Samsung has been without regrets and that your Galaxy S25 FE has been performing flawlessly! Equipped with the Exynos 2400, Samsung’s flagship performance processor, this device is built to deliver ultra-smooth gaming and faster responsiveness, while also offering great value for money.       Response from Samsung:
      2026-08-31

      Samsung

      Congratulations on your upgrade, David! We're delighted to hear that you're enjoying your new Galaxy S25 FE and that the transfer from your A55 was largely successful. When you use Smart Switch to move to a new device, it copies your apps, layouts and credentials, but it can't copy your private email database or custom subfolders. Not to worry, as these are safely stored with your email provider and can be synced over. Open the Samsung Email app > Tap the three horizontal lines (Menu) in the top-left corner > Settings icon (gear symbol) > Tap on your specific email account > Email sync period > Change this to 'All time'. If you're using a different email app, the steps may be slightly different. We can provide you with detailed steps for most email apps, so don't hesitate to reach out to our Support Teams using the contact details and opening times here: https://www.samsung.com/uk/support/contact/ Thank you for taking the time to share your review, and we hope this information is helpful. ^EW at Samsung Support

      Response from Samsung:
      2026-06-01

      Samsung

      We're sorry to see that you're having some issues with Face recognition on your S25 FE, Nikki, along with restoring your data. We'd love to help. You can restore your Samsung Cloud backups by going to Settings > Accounts and backup > Samsung Cloud > Restore data > Your S25 FE. For your Samsung Notes app, you'll need to ensure that your notes are synced with the cloud. You can do this by opening the Notes app > Tap the 3 lines on the left > Tap the Settings cog > Toggle on Sync with Samsung Cloud. Please note that this must be turned on for any backups to occur. For the Face recognition, please wipe your front camera lens with a soft, clean microfiber cloth and remove any obstructions which may be covering this area, such as a case or screen protector. Re-register your face by going to Settings > Lock screen and AOD > Screen lock and biometrics > Enter your PIN/password > Face recognition > Remove face data > Register face > Continue. If you struggle in low light conditions, within the Face recognition sub menu above, please Toggle Brighten the screen to On. This will temporarily light up the display to illuminate your face when using Face recognition. You can use the Add alternative appearance feature to register different looks such as glasses, hats, make-up, or facial hair. You can find further information and steps on the following link: https://www.samsung.com/uk/support/mobile-devices/what-to-do-if-facial-recognition-isnt-working-on-your-galaxy-phone/ For your contactless payments, please check out the following link, which contains a really handy guide with pictures to resolve any issues regarding making payments: https://www.samsung.com/uk/support/mobile-devices/troubleshoot-nfc-issues-on-galaxy-devices/ We hope this information is helpful for you, and if you need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach back out to our Support Teams using the contact details and opening times on the following link: https://www.samsung.com/uk/support/contact/ ^EW at Samsung Support

      • After 24 Months
        If you haven’t upgraded
        Pay the final instalment to keep your phone. Return it and upgrade. Or, return it and we’ll settle your final payment.
